style: For this selected reading say ar-ti-ZAN: put the main beat on the FINAL syllable ZAN /zæn/, which must be stronger than the initial /ɑː/. The initial AR has secondary stress only. Do not substitute the also-existing first-stressed reading. Keep three connected syllables in one natural word, with a clear final /zæn/, not /zən/. This guidance is not part of the spoken transcript.

Use the British LOT vowel /ɒ/ in /wɒn/, as in British want without its final /t/. Do not use the STRUT vowel /ʌ/ of the usual pronunciation of one, or the American /ɑ/. Say one connected monosyllable, without reading this guidance or the comparison words.
